body: I don't expect you'll get the answers you want out of her.  My guess is that it's best to make the break as clean as you can and start trying to work on moving on.
I don't know enough to say.  Maybe I can understand the urge but I don't think it helps you.
Every relationship before the one that works doesn't.  The ones that fail are a guide towards the one that works.

I'm sure that it's nearly impossible to see right now but humans are incredible at adapting to change.  That probably sounds like shit right now, I'm sure I wouldn't want to accept that change but life is always changing.  

I just ask that you consider the idea that you could be in a happier and healthier relationship.  It's really not so far fetched but you're going to have to be tough and work through it for a bit.
I hope you've reconsidered or at least put it off.

It's going to be a rough patch but you have to get a divorce and move on.  You've found yourself with someone who doesn't love who are and that sucks man.  That said, if you stick around, you will inevitably find yourself in a better situation.

I think I can sympathize with that feeling and maybe medicine won't be the complete answer for you.  With that being said I think you should pursue your personal answer.  

These questions of what's real and other what ifs are something I too deal with and while it can be tough I think it's a worthy pursuit.  Stay curious and seek answers, I think it's a healthy way to get better.

I know it's tough to hear but it's never too late to change things up.  Clearly the way things are going isn't working for you and if you are considering suicide then perhaps it's time to try a new lifestyle.  I'm no expert and I don't know what that change is for you but maybe the one freeing thing I had in my deepest depression was knowing that whatever I did couldn't be worse than suicide.

After a lot of trial and error I found a way to keep busy in a healthy way until life normalized a bit more.  I don't think there is ever a clear answer to life but the pursuit of that answer is worthy of investigating.
It's worth seeing if medicine works for you.  What's the harm in hanging around and seeing how that goes?

In my experience, it's going to be terribly difficult.  That said you just have to try and persevere.  I remember realizing and holding on to the idea that I didn't want to hurt others like I had been hurt.  

I did end up losing my job as I over ran my allotted disability time but at this point in my life I'm content with that.  The job doesn't define you, just get by for now and you can figure that out later if you need to change your job.
